name: TrueUSD
oneLiner: TUSD is a centralized dollar stablecoin from Techteryx with a Chainlink Proof-of-Reserve feed, though current reserves sit in opaque First Digital Trust funds.
collateral: Daily Moore Hong Kong / Chainlink-attested TUSD reserves, currently modeled by Pharos as concentrated in opaque First Digital Trust fund investments with a small cash-at-depository-institutions balance.
pegMechanism: Direct 1:1 redemption through Techteryx; minting controlled by Chainlink Proof of Reserve feed preventing supply from exceeding attested reserves

sources.label: Moore CPA Independent Assurance Report on the TUSD Consolidated Reserves Report - July 22, 2026

applicabilityBasis.summary: TUSD is a U.S. dollar-pegged stablecoin with issuer-managed redemption and daily reserve attestations.

genius.notes: Techteryx (current TUSD issuer, BVI-incorporated) has no confirmed U.S. GENIUS approval, application, or foreign-issuer exception. The SEC settled charges in September 2024 against prior TUSD operators TrueCoin LLC and TrustToken Inc. for false reserve representations through April 2023; Techteryx was not named, so this is tracked as a warning/notice posture rather than a prohibited/revoked current-issuer action. Ongoing civil litigation in Hong Kong and Dubai (worldwide asset freeze of $456M tied to First Digital Trust/Aria Commodities reserve dispute) does not constitute a U.S. enforcement action against Techteryx. TUSD delisted from EEA-regulated venues by Q1 2025 (Kraken, Binance) and several Binance spot pairs delisted April 2026.

mintAuthority.summary: TUSD has four independently mintable issuer-native deployments. Ethereum uses a 2/3 Safe, BSC and Avalanche use chain-local 2/3 Safes with the same three owners, and Tron uses a single native account. Each final owner can bypass the configured mint pools and approvals, replace the mint key, and immediately upgrade both the token and controller proxies.

sources.label: TrueUSD supported contracts and native deployments

controls.label: TUSD issuer-native owner authority set
controls.capDescription: Unbounded at zero on-chain delay. Any one of the three independent effective authority domains can request and finalize an owner mint without pool subtraction, reset limits or mint keys, or replace mint-critical logic.
bypassSurfaces: Ethereum Safe can use owner-only requestMint/finalizeMint and upgrade both custom proxies.
Tron controller owner is a single native account with the same direct-mint and upgrade bypass.
BSC and Avalanche use separate Safes but the same 2-of-3 signer set, which can mint and upgrade on either chain.

sources.label: TrueUSD supported contracts and native deployments

controls.evidence: This umbrella record exists because the upgradeability schema accepts one controlRef. It does not represent one shared signer or quorum. It preserves three effective failure domains: the Ethereum 2/3 Safe, the Tron 1/1 native account, and the common 2/3 signer set behind the BSC and Avalanche Safes. Each deployment's controller owner can request any amount and finalize it as owner without approval or pool checks.

controls.label: Tron TUSD controller owner and proxy-admin account
bypassSurfaces: Owner-only requestMint/finalizeMint bypasses ratifier approvals and all three mint pools.
The same account owns the controller proxy and can route token-proxy upgrades through the controller.

The latest indexed controller transaction was block 83560002, before the cutoff, so the directly read state was unchanged through the anchor.

review.evidence: Exact-cutoff review used Ethereum block 25526129, Tron block 84434937, BSC block 109812367, and Avalanche block 90233120. On every native deployment the token proxy owner was its TokenController proxy, while the final controller owner also owned the controller proxy. The controller source permits owner requestMint/finalizeMint without approval or pool subtraction and owner-controlled mint-key, threshold, limit, and proxy upgrades. Ethereum was a 2/3 Safe; Tron was a 1/1 native account; BSC and Avalanche were separate 2/3 Safes sharing all three owners. No enabled Safe modules, guards, module guards, or timelocks were found. The smaller Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, and Fantom contracts remain separately scoped as unresolved bridge routes rather than being asserted as issuer-native mint paths.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: TrueUSD has four issuer-native mintable deployments (Ethereum, BSC, Avalanche, Tron) whose controllers match the reviewed mintAuthority profile; the Polygon, Arbitrum, and Optimism deployments are canonical-bridge lock-mint representations (Polygon PoS ChildChainManager, Arbitrum L2ERC20Gateway, OP L2StandardBridge), the Fantom deployment is a legacy Multichain representation controlled by the defunct Multichain MPC EOA, and the NEAR deployment is a Rainbow Bridge factory representation.

On-chain 2026-07-20: l1Address() returns the canonical Ethereum TUSD 0x0000000000085d4780b73119b644ae5ecd22b376 and l2Gateway() returns the Arbitrum L2ERC20Gateway 0x09e9222E96E7B4AE2a407B98d48e330053351EEe, which is the sole bridgeMint authority for this standard L2 representation; L1GatewayRouter.l1TokenToGateway maps TUSD to the standard L1ERC20Gateway.

On-chain 2026-07-20: l1Token() returns the canonical Ethereum TUSD 0x0000000000085d4780b73119b644ae5ecd22b376 and l2Bridge() returns the predeployed L2StandardBridge 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000010, the sole mint authority for this standard L2 representation.

owner() read on-chain 2026-07-20 returns the issuer controller 0xb25e3c3493fc61bdd02661bcc27058022716c66a, matching the reviewed mintAuthority profile; issuer-native deployment, no bridge control carries the claim.

owner() read on-chain 2026-07-20 returns the Multichain MPC EOA 0xc564ee9f21ed8a2d8e7e76c085740d5e4c5fafbe (no contract code), so this is a legacy Multichain lock-mint representation whose mint/upgrade authority is the defunct Multichain MPC key set; Multichain ceased operations in July 2023, so remaining supply is a stranded representation with an unresponsive controller.

NEAR RPC reads 2026-07-20 confirm this NEP-141 (name TrueUSD, ~510k supply) is a Rainbow Bridge factory-minted subaccount of factory.bridge.near, which is the sole mint/burn authority on NEAR against proofs of lock in the Ethereum-side locker.

notices.title: Material issuer and market-stability risks
notices.message: TrueUSD has multiple unresolved 2025-2026 risk events: Archblock filed Chapter 11 on February 6, 2026; Kraken scheduled TUSD delisting with remaining balances liquidated on March 1, 2026; S&P Global assigned TUSD its weakest stablecoin stability score of 5 on November 14, 2025; and the DIFC Digital Economy Court issued a worldwide freezing injunction up to USD 456M in Techteryx-related reserve litigation.
